concurrency_primitives: std::thread::scope (5 files concurrently, borrowed interners); per-file reader thread -> crossbeam_channel::bounded(parsers*2) -> N parser threads with buffer-pool return channel; RwLock<HashMap> interner; rayon par_iter_mut/fold/reduce/join for matching and vote tallies; rayon par_chunks map-reduce for neighborhood aggregates; Vec<AtomicU32> fetch_add for block counters; par_sort_unstable; five questions via par_iter over Box<dyn Question> in a private rayon ThreadPool; deterministic output verified 1 vs 10 threads; no unsafe
design_patterns: Builder (PipelineBuilder::build validates once), Pipeline (4 stages passing ownership), Strategy (MatchStrategy, Question, Renderer, CsvSchema traits), Factory (report::renderer(format), analysis::questions(ids)); all realized in code
questions: Where do vacant buildings and violent crime overlap, and how strongly does one track the other? (Mayor's Office, HCD; neighborhood + block joins)
Do blocks with liquor outlets see more violent crime than comparable blocks, and which licensed blocks stand out? (Liquor Board, BPD; block-address join)
How much violent crime happens beyond the reach of the CitiWatch camera network, and where would new cameras see the most? (BPD, MONSE; 150 m spatial join + city map)
Where is resident-reported blight concentrated, and do high-vacancy neighborhoods wait longer for it to be resolved? (DPW, HCD; 311 x vacants)
Taking violence, vacancy, blight, camera coverage and liquor outlets together, which neighborhoods need coordinated investment first? (Mayor's Office, Planning; all five datasets)
stakeholders: Mayor's Office of Neighborhood Safety and Engagement
overview: A 4,330-line Rust crate organized as a four-stage pipeline (ingest -> match -> aggregate -> analyse) with a validated PipelineBuilder, Strategy traits for schemas, matching, questions and renderers, and factories for the latter two. Ingestion streams 4 MiB quote-aware chunks through bounded crossbeam channels into parser threads that emit compact Copy records with interned ids; matching recovers missing neighborhoods via spatial cells and hundred-block address keys; rayon map-reduce and atomics build the aggregates; questions run in parallel and render to terminal, HTML (SVG maps), JSON and an optional localhost server. Clippy-clean, no unsafe, 28 tests including an end-to-end hand-built city, and a README whose every claim verified.
stakeholder_value: The five questions are genuinely cross-dataset and use three different join grains (neighborhood name, hundred-block address, 150 m spatial radius), yielding specific, actionable outputs: outlet blocks carry 17.6% of violence on 5.5% of blocks even within the same neighborhood, 41.5% of violent crime is out of camera range with ten named candidate sites, high-vacancy neighborhoods are not served slower on blight requests (an equity check with a clear answer), and a weighted priority index assigns a lead agency per neighborhood. Methods and limits (raw counts, correlation not causation, mismatched data periods) are stated in each section.
issues: Datasets cover different periods (crime 2022-2026, 311 2025 only, vacant notices back to 2010) and nothing is per-resident normalized; disclosed but affects Q1/Q5 comparability
Hand-rolled DST/calendar and map-projection code instead of established crates; well-tested but more to maintain
--serve is a one-line HTTP parser serving a single in-memory page (fine for the assignment, not production)
First cargo build requires network to fetch crates; no run.sh (README relies on cargo run --release)
Q5 index weights are an undocumented-sensitivity judgment call
rationale: Every rubric criterion is met at its top tier and was verified: five real bundled datasets plus a fetch script, a warning-free release build and clippy, 28 passing tests, a 0.92 s full run at 217 MB RSS with HTML/JSON/terminal output and a curl-verified web server, concurrency in every stage that is deterministic across thread counts with no unsafe, realized Builder/Strategy/Factory/Pipeline patterns, and five substantive cross-dataset questions with actionable findings. Remaining issues are disclosed limitations rather than specification failures. Total 100, A.
